candidates.label: toLocation

Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: studyLocation

Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: location

candidates.label: contentLocation

candidates.label: fromLocation

Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: pattern
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the visual or design pattern of a creative work or product. Also called design, motif, print, style. Examples: A dress has a pattern of 'polka dot'. A fabric has a pattern of 'striped'. A flag has a pattern of 'Canadian flag'.

candidates.label: isConsumableFor
candidates.comment: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

candidates.label: isPlanForApartment
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a floor plan and the accommodation unit it illustrates. Also called plan for, describes accommodation, layout for. Examples: A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Apartment 3B'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'a studio apartment'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Unit 101'.

chosen_property.justification: The 'potentialAction' property fits ConditionalImprovement (subtype of Thing) having an Action as a potential activity.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: hasMolecularFunction
candidates.comment: A molecular function relation between a biochemical entity and its performed molecular function. Also called performs function, molecular role, functional activity. Examples: "A protein has a molecular function of enzyme activity.", "This BioChemEntity has a molecular function described by a defined term.", "The entity's molecular function is specified."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: interactionCount
candidates.comment: A deprecated property indicating the number of user interactions with an item. Also called user interactions, engagement count, activity count. Examples: (No active examples for deprecated properties).

candidates.label: hasMeasurement
candidates.comment: A measurement relation between a certification, offer, product, or size specification and a quantitative value representing a specific measurement. Also called item measurement, dimension, size value. Examples: "A product has a measurement for its height.", "An offer includes a measurement for package weight.", "The certification has a measurement of carbon footprint."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: muscleAction
candidates.comment: A description of the movement generated by a muscle. Also called muscle function, muscle movement, action of muscle. Examples: "Biceps Brachii muscleAction 'flexion of elbow'", "Triceps Brachii muscleAction 'extension of elbow'", "Deltoid muscleAction 'abduction of shoulder'".

candidates.label: activityDuration
candidates.comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."

candidates.label: mechanismOfAction
candidates.comment: A mechanism of action relation between a dietary supplement or drug and the specific biochemical interaction producing its pharmacological effect. Also called: mode of action, pharmacological mechanism, how it works. Examples: "Aspirin mechanismOfAction 'Inhibits COX enzymes'", "Insulin mechanismOfAction 'Binds to insulin receptors'", "Antidepressant mechanismOfAction 'Increases serotonin levels'".

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

chosen_property.definition: Describes a condition that was not known or experienced during a specific time period.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org candidate property fits 'WeatherCondition -> Duration' for describing a previously unknown condition.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: drug
candidates.comment: A drug relation between a medical entity (such as a drug class, condition, patient, or therapeutic procedure) and a specific drug or medicine. Also called "medication used", "prescribed drug", "contains drug". Examples: "Medical condition 'Hypertension' drug 'Lisinopril'", "Therapeutic procedure 'Chemotherapy' drug 'Paclitaxel'", "Drug class 'Statins' drug 'Atorvastatin'".

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

chosen_property.label: eventStatus
chosen_property.justification: The 'eventStatus' property fits Schedule (subtype of Event) with a StatusEnumeration (subtype of EventStatusType) as its state.

candidates.label: itemCondition
candidates.comment: A product state relation indicating the physical condition of a product or service, or the condition required for returns. Also called product state, condition of item, quality status, return condition. Examples: An offer has an itemCondition of 'NewCondition'. A product has an itemCondition of 'UsedCondition'. A return policy specifies itemCondition 'SellerRefurbished'.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: legalStatus
candidates.comment: A regulatory status relation between a dietary supplement, drug, or medical entity and its legal classification, including controlled substance schedules. Also called regulatory status, legal classification, controlled substance status, drug schedule. Examples: A drug has a legalStatus of 'PrescriptionOnly'. A dietary supplement has a legalStatus of 'OverTheCounter'. A medication has a legalStatus of 'Schedule II controlled substance'. Distinct from drugClass, which is a medical classification, not a legal one.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: prescriptionStatus
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the prescription status of a drug, such as whether it is prescription-only or over-the-counter. Also called drug availability, dispensing status, OTC/Rx status. Examples: A drug has a prescription status of 'PrescriptionOnly'. The medication has a prescription status of 'OverTheCounter'. This drug's prescription status is 'ControlledSubstance'.

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."
